biophysical_burden.boundary: Currently mapped salt-affected soil; the additional area at risk is excluded.

human_economic_burden.boundary: FAO estimate of lost crop production in irrigated salt-degraded areas; population context is not added.

persistence.boundary: Earlier FAO assessment synthesis of recurring annual farmland loss; not a current annual panel.

extent.global_extent_context: Global land assessment with salt-affected soils on all continents and explicit irrigated and rainfed cropland estimates

source_locators.biophysical_burden: FAO 2024 release: 1,381 million hectares, or 10.7 percent of global land, are salt-affected.
source_locators.human_economic_burden: FAO Global Soil Partnership: global annual cost of salt-induced land degradation in irrigated areas is estimated at US$27.3 billion in lost crop production.
source_locators.persistence: FAO Global Soil Partnership: salinization takes up to 1.5 million hectares of farmland out of production each year.
source_locators.extent: FAO Global Soil Partnership: salt-affected soils occur on all continents; the 2024 assessment reports global irrigated and rainfed cropland shares.
source_locators.human_context: FAO Global Soil Partnership 2021 map release: more than 1.5 billion people face significant food-growing challenges associated with saline irrigated soils.

excluded_from_scoring: one billion additional hectares at risk, which is not added to currently affected area
upper-bound crop-yield losses in the most affected countries, which are not a global mean
population challenge context, which is retained but not added to the monetary burden
future 24 to 32 percent land-area projections
unreported uncertainty as zero

transformations.formula: Normalize 1,381 million currently affected hectares through declared area anchors; exclude one billion hectares at risk.
Normalize the FAO annual crop-production-loss estimate without adding population exposure or projected losses.
Normalize the source-reported annual farmland area taken out of production.
Normalize the mapped share of global land while retaining all-continent scope and spatial heterogeneity.

receipts.uncertainty: The 2024 global map combines heterogeneous national inventories, remote sensing, soil surveys and models. Natural salinity and human-induced salinization are not fully separable everywhere. The annual land-loss and crop-cost estimates come from earlier assessment syntheses and are not a current observation series. Irrigated-land and population exposure do not imply uniform yield loss.
receipts.freshness: FAO global salt-affected-soils assessment 2024; earlier annual cost and land-loss syntheses retained with caveats; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T21:32:51.837Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: FAO quantifies accumulated salt-affected area, crop-production cost, recurring annual farmland loss and global land extent under explicit boundaries.
higher_priority_failures: The assessment is not a source-consistent current global annual field-salinity panel with magnitude plus threshold or momentum.
The annual land-loss estimate is an assessment synthesis and is therefore retained as persistence evidence rather than relabeled current data.

biophysical_burden.boundary: All UNEP reactive-nitrogen losses to the environment, including leaching to soil, rivers and lakes; overlapping pathways are not added.

human_economic_burden.boundary: Global annual lost-nitrogen resource cost; not a water-only damage estimate.

persistence.boundary: Duration of the documented global dead-zone inventory increase; not a continuous severity series.

extent.geographic_scope: Worldwide nutrient losses to air, soil, rivers, lakes, marine and coastal systems; coastal eutrophication and dead-zone inventories are global lower bounds
extent.boundary: UNEP worldwide lower-bound inventory; no unmonitored area is classified.

source_locators.biophysical_burden: UNEP nitrogen facts: 200 million tonnes of reactive nitrogen, or 80 percent, is lost to the environment each year, including leaching to soil, rivers and lakes.
source_locators.economic_burden: UNEP nitrogen facts: annual cost of lost nitrogen resources is estimated at around US$200 billion.
source_locators.agricultural_runoff: UNEP agricultural-runoff summary: more than half of nitrogen applied to farmland washes into rivers rather than being absorbed by crops.
source_locators.eutrophication_extent: UNEP nutrient-management issue: more than 500 coastal areas worldwide are impacted by eutrophication caused by excess nutrients.
source_locators.persistence: UNEP nutrient-management issue: documented ocean dead zones increased from 10 in 1960 to 405 in 2008.
source_locators.fisheries_exposure: UNEP nutrient-management issue: more than 90 percent of world fisheries depend in some way on estuarine and near-shore habitats.

excluded_from_scoring: regional European nutrient-pollution cost ranges
United States-only eutrophication costs
dead-zone count converted to area or volume
fisheries dependence treated as realized loss
reactive-nitrogen pathways added across overlapping budgets
unreported uncertainty as zero

transformations.formula: Normalize only the node-matched UNEP mass, share or affected-system count through declared anchors.
Normalize the source-reported global nitrogen-resource cost or fisheries-system exposure without allocating it to a locality or treating exposure as realized loss.
Normalize the 48-year interval over which UNEP reports the global dead-zone inventory rose from 10 to 405.
Use the source-declared worldwide assessment scope; retain site counts as lower bounds and never convert them to area.

receipts.uncertainty: Reactive-nitrogen budgets combine air, soil, freshwater and marine pathways. The annual resource-cost estimate is global nitrogen loss, not an allocated water-pollution damage value. Coastal-system inventories depend on monitoring and definitions and therefore are lower bounds. Fisheries dependence is economic-system exposure, not realized attributable loss.
receipts.freshness: UNEP global nutrient-management findings reviewed 2024; underlying budgets and inventories have different assessment years; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T21:51:19.347Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: UNEP quantifies annual global reactive-nitrogen loss, the associated resource cost, multi-decade dead-zone accumulation and worldwide aquatic extent.
